content: 1. The concurrent use of anticholinergic drugs may result in a diminished response to stimulation testing with secretin. To mitigate this effect, it is recommended to discontinue anticholinergic drugs at least five half-lives prior to administering secretin. 2. Flavoxate reduces the efficacy of secretin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. It is advised to avoid or use an alternative drug in such cases. 3. Glycopyrrolate decreases the effects of secretin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or consider alternative medications. 4. Hyoscyamine diminishes the effects of secretin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Discontinue hyoscyamine at least five half-lives before secretin administration. 5. Hyoscyamine spray also reduces the effects of secretin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. The combination of ibuprofen and famotidine with secretin may lead to a hyperresponse in gastrin secretion during stimulation testing, falsely suggesting gastrinoma. Discontinue H2-receptor antagonists at least two days before secretin administration to aid in accurate diagnosis. 7. Lansoprazole may cause a hyperresponse in gastrin secretion during stimulation testing with secretin, potentially leading to a false diagnosis of gastrinoma. Temporarily stop lansoprazole treatment at least 30 days before testing to allow gastrin levels to return to baseline. 8. Meclizine reduces the effects of secretin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Methscopolamine decreases the efficacy of secretin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Discontinue methscopolamine at least five half-lives before secretin administration. 10. Nizatidine, an H2-receptor antagonist, may cause a hyperresponse in gastrin secretion during stimulation testing with secretin, falsely suggesting gastrinoma. Discontinue nizatidine at least two days before secretin administration. 11. Omeprazole may lead to a hyperresponse in gastrin secretion during stimulation testing with secretin, potentially resulting in a false diagnosis of gastrinoma. Temporarily stop omeprazole treatment at least 14 days before testing to allow gastrin levels to normalize. 12. Oxybutynin reduces the effects of secretin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Oxybutynin topical and transdermal formulations also decrease the effects of secretin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Discontinue these medications at least five half-lives before secretin administration. 14. Pantoprazole may cause elevated gastrin levels to persist for up to three months following short-term treatment. Discontinue pantoprazole well in advance of secretin testing to allow gastrin levels to return to baseline. 15. Propantheline reduces the effects of secretin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Rabeprazole may cause a hyperresponse in gastrin secretion during stimulation testing with secretin, falsely suggesting gastrinoma. Discontinue rabeprazole sufficiently in advance to allow gastrin levels to normalize. 17. Scopolamine diminishes the effects of secretin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Discontinue scopolamine at least five half-lives before secretin administration. 18. Solifenacin reduces the efficacy of secretin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Tolterodine decreases the effects of secretin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Discontinue tolterodine at least five half-lives before secretin administration. 20. Trihexyphenidyl reduces the effects of secretin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Trospium chloride diminishes the efficacy of secretin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Discontinue trospium chloride at least five half-lives before secretin administration. 22. Co-administration of H2-receptor antagonists or proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) with secretin may cause a hyperresponse in gastrin secretion during stimulation testing, falsely suggesting gastrinoma. Discontinue H2-receptor antagonists at least two days and PPIs for a duration specific to the individual PPI before secretin administration. 23. There is no available data on the use of synthetic human secretin in pregnant women, and animal reproduction studies have not been conducted. The presence of synthetic human secretin in human or animal milk is also unknown. 24. Reconstitute secretin with 9% NaCl, ensuring complete dissolution by vigorous shaking. Inspect the solution for particulate matter or discoloration before administration. If abnormalities are observed, discard the solution. Use immediately after reconstitution and discard any unused portion. 25. Administer secretin via slow intravenous injection over one minute. Store the product frozen at -20°C and protect it from light. 26. Formulary information may vary by individual plans and is subject to change. Contact the applicable plan provider for the most current information.
